assertion.statement: For the actual rational homomorphism rho:U->G, one positive integer D can be chosen so that rho(exp(D L0)) is contained in Gamma, while remaining divisible by the integer already required for BCH closure.
assertion.objects: The fixed simply connected nilpotent U and G, rational homomorphism rho, homogeneous rational basis of Lie(U), its integer span L0, and a rational Malcev basis of G adapted to Gamma.
assertion.hypotheses: The preceding construction supplies rational rho and the stated rational bases. BCH closure and cocompactness of exp(D L0) are supplied separately by the displayed local proof.
assertion.quantifiers: Every x in L0 for one D chosen from the finitely many coordinate polynomials of this fixed construction.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed finite-dimensional nilpotent groups and fixed rational bases; no varying-family denominator estimate.
assertion.uniformity: The same D works for all integer coordinate vectors x in L0 within this fixed construction.
assertion.constants: D is a common positive multiple of coordinate-polynomial denominators and the prior BCH denominator requirement.
assertion.normalizations: Second-kind Malcev coordinates identify Gamma exactly with integer vectors; rho(exp x)=exp(d rho(x)).
assertion.exceptional_cases: Every coordinate polynomial has zero constant term because rho maps identity to identity. Thus scaling variables by D clears denominators in every nonzero-degree monomial; no assertion that an arbitrary polynomial with nonintegral constant can be so scaled.
assertion.limit_order: Fix rho and bases; write the finite rational coordinate polynomials; choose one common multiple D; then evaluate on every integer vector. Increasing D preserves denominator divisibility.

use.reason: Apply the already reviewed GT12 coordinate conversion to the actual rational rho, then clear finitely many denominators in positive-degree monomials as proved in LP02.
